title: The Perfect Witness
premise: Estate lawyer Theo Sterling, the quiet keeper of Marlow Bend's secrets, is hired by a dying client to prove that local matriarch Vivian Ashford will be murdered in eleven days — a crime that hasn't happened yet, predicted with chilling specificity. As Theo investigates, he uncovers a five-year-old 'closed' case: the drowning of Vivian's son, ruled accidental, whose true killer is one of the town's most powerful men. The premonition is real — it comes from the killer himself, who plans to finish what he started before the statute of limitations expires and a hidden witness can testify. In the end, Theo must choose between the law he serves and justice it failed, staging an elaborate trap on the night of the predicted murder that forces a confession, saves Vivian, and finally gives the dead boy his voice.
about_author: Rosalind Brightwater spent fifteen years as a probate clerk in small-town New England before turning to fiction, where she learned that every filing cabinet holds at least one body. She writes mysteries about ordinary professionals who discover the paperwork of power.

chapters.title: The Will That Wasn't
chapters.summary: Theo Sterling, POV. A stranger named Elias Crane hires Theo to witness a will for a woman who isn't dead yet — and pays triple to prove her murder hasn't happened. Theo's careful invisibility cracks as curiosity wins. Beat: uneasy fascination.

chapters.title: Marlow Bend, Alphabetized
chapters.summary: Theo, POV. Establishing his methodical life: files, routines, five years of keeping the town's secrets neatly shelved after a scandal ended his career. He researches Crane and finds nothing. Beat: controlled unease deepening into obsession.

chapters.title: Eleven Days
chapters.summary: Theo, POV. Crane's prediction is precise: Vivian Ashford dies October 14th, drowned in her own bath. Theo visits the Ashford estate under pretext of estate planning and meets Vivian — sharp, grieving, guarded. Beat: first contact with danger.

chapters.title: The Drowned Boy
chapters.summary: Vivian, POV. Five years ago her son Daniel drowned; the town called it an accident. She reveals she received the same letter Theo did — someone wants her terrified before she dies. Beat: grief weaponized into dread.

chapters.title: Closed for Good
chapters.summary: Theo, POV. He pulls Daniel Ashford's case file from the sheriff's office and finds it suspiciously thin: no autopsy photos, a witness statement signed by a man who'd left town years earlier. Beat: the first hard evidence something was buried.

chapters.title: The Sheriff's Signature
chapters.summary: Sheriff Dale Pruitt, POV. Pruitt remembers closing the case fast, on orders he didn't question. Now Theo is asking questions, and a call from county judge Raymond Hobb tells him to make it stop. Beat: complicity and fear.

chapters.title: Crane's Confession
chapters.summary: Theo, POV. Theo confronts Crane, who admits he isn't a prophet — he's the killer's former accountant, holding ledgers that prove payments to Pruitt dated the week Daniel died. Beat: revelation that reframes everything.

chapters.title: What the Ledger Buys
chapters.summary: Crane, POV. Flashback: Crane laundered hush money for developer Marcus Vane for a decade, including the Ashford payment. Dying of cancer, Crane wants absolution the law can't give. Beat: guilt seeking redemption.

chapters.title: Statute of Limitations
chapters.summary: Theo, POV. Theo learns the murder statute expires in twelve days — the same window as the prediction. The killer isn't prophesying; he's counting down to legal safety. Beat: the trap reveals its shape.

chapters.title: Vane of the Valley
chapters.summary: Theo, POV. Theo attends a charity gala and studies Marcus Vane — charming philanthropist, half-owner of the town. Vane recognizes him and offers a retainer, a velvet threat. Beat: menace wrapped in courtesy.

chapters.title: The Widow's Memory
chapters.summary: Vivian, POV. Vivian recalls Daniel's last night: he'd argued with someone at the marina, someone he trusted. She gives Theo a name she never told police — but it's not Vane's. Beat: hope tangled with confusion.

chapters.title: Pruitt's Price
chapters.summary: Pruitt, POV. Vane pressures Pruitt to arrest Crane on old fraud charges, silencing the ledger. Pruitt hesitates — Crane has insurance, copies everywhere. Beat: the corrupt machine grinding against its own parts.

chapters.title: Seven Days
chapters.summary: Theo, POV. Crane is arrested anyway; the ledger vanishes from evidence. Theo realizes he's now the only person holding the thread, and Vane knows it. Beat: isolation and rising stakes.

chapters.title: A Witness Who Saw Nothing
chapters.summary: Theo, POV. Theo tracks down Ruth Calloway, the marina waitress whose statement closed the case. She admits she lied — paid, then threatened — and saw Vane's boat that night. Beat: the buried witness surfaces.

chapters.title: Ruth's Silence
chapters.summary: Ruth, POV. Ruth explains why she recanted: they had her brother's parole in their hands. She'll testify only if Vivian is protected first. Beat: fear negotiating with conscience.

chapters.title: The Safe House Problem
chapters.summary: Theo, POV. Theo moves Ruth and Vivian to a motel under false names, using estate-law sleight of hand to hide the paper trail. His invisible-man skills become weapons. Beat: competence as catharsis.

chapters.title: Hobb's Chambers
chapters.summary: Judge Raymond Hobb, POV. Hobb, who quashed the original autopsy, feels the walls closing in and considers flipping on Vane — but Vane holds recordings of them both. Beat: corruption devouring itself.

chapters.title: Five Days
chapters.summary: Theo, POV. Someone ransacks Theo's office; every file on the Ashfords is gone, but nothing else touched. A message, not a burglary. Beat: violation and clarity — this is personal now.

chapters.title: The Second Letter
chapters.summary: Vivian, POV. Vivian receives a new letter: 'October 14th. You'll understand why.' She stops being a victim-in-waiting and starts helping Theo plan. Beat: grief transmuted into resolve.

chapters.title: Daniel's Boat
chapters.summary: Theo, POV. Theo dives into county records and finds Daniel had recently discovered discrepancies in Vane's marina development — land fraud worth millions. Motive established. Beat: the puzzle clicking together.

chapters.title: What Ruth Really Saw
chapters.summary: Ruth, POV. Under Theo's gentle questioning, Ruth recalls more: Daniel wasn't alone on the pier. There was a second figure — someone who helped pull him from the water too late. Beat: memory's cruel precision.

chapters.title: The Accomplice Question
chapters.summary: Theo, POV. If someone helped drown Daniel, the accomplice may be the letter-writer — someone consumed by guilt, not malice. Theo re-reads Crane's letters and finds a phrase only a witness would use. Beat: paradigm shift.

chapters.title: Crane in Custody
chapters.summary: Crane, POV. From jail, Crane admits the truth: he was on the pier that night, watched Vane hold Daniel under, and ran. The letters were his penance — forcing the town to look before time ran out. Beat: confession as expiation.

chapters.title: Three Days
chapters.summary: Theo, POV. With Crane jailed and Ruth terrified, Theo stands nearly alone. He drafts two documents: a sworn affidavit for Ruth, and — if all else fails — his own resignation letter. Beat: the loneliest hour.

chapters.title: Pruitt Breaks
chapters.summary: Pruitt, POV. Pruitt finds the missing ledger returned to his desk with a note: 'Your copy.' Realizing Vane intends to burn everyone including him, Pruitt makes a choice and calls Theo. Beat: the first domino falls.

chapters.title: The Devil's Retainer
chapters.summary: Theo, POV. Vane summons Theo and offers him partnership, wealth, and the case file destroyed — everything Theo lost five years ago, restored. Theo says yes. Beat: the reader's heart stops.

chapters.title: Double Blind
chapters.summary: Theo, POV. Theo's acceptance was theater: he wore a wire borrowed from a state investigator Pruitt secretly contacted. But Vane never said anything incriminating — he's too careful. Beat: hope dashed, plan B required.

chapters.title: The Marina at Night
chapters.summary: Ruth, POV. Ruth agrees to walk the pier where Daniel died and reconstruct her testimony on record. Mid-interview, headlights sweep the lot — someone is watching. Beat: terror in open air.

chapters.title: Two Days
chapters.summary: Theo, POV. Theo realizes Vane must act before the statute expires — the 14th isn't just a threat, it's his deadline. Whatever happens, it happens at the Ashford house. Beat: the trap inverted — now Theo sets it.

chapters.title: Invitation to a Murder
chapters.summary: Vivian, POV. On Theo's advice, Vivian publicly announces a gala at the estate on the 14th — celebrating the fifth anniversary of Daniel's memorial foundation. Bait laid. Beat: defiance dressed as hospitality.

chapters.title: Every Alibi Money Can Buy
chapters.summary: Theo, POV. Theo maps Vane's likely play: not violence, but a staged accident or a poisoned inheritance — and discovers Vane quietly bought Vivian's medication supplier last month. Beat: cold horror at the banality of the plot.

chapters.title: Swapping the Poison
chapters.summary: Theo, POV. Theo and Pruitt intercept the tampered medication, replace it with inert tablets, and set the scene: on the 14th, Vane will believe his plan worked. Beat: quiet, surgical tension.

chapters.title: The Night Of
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs interwoven. The gala proceeds; Vane works the room; Vivian takes her pills before the guests; Theo watches the clock. At 9:47, Vivian collapses. Beat: the predicted moment arrives.

chapters.title: Confession at the Deathbed
chapters.summary: Vane, POV. Believing Vivian dying, Vane leans close to gloat — and the room's doors open. Doctors, a stenographer, a state trooper, and a recording device. Vivian opens her eyes. Beat: the mask torn off.

chapters.title: What the Law Heard
chapters.summary: Theo, POV. The confession is damning but Vane's lawyers move instantly to suppress it. Then Ruth's affidavit, Pruitt's testimony, and Hobb's flipped cooperation stack the weight of the town itself against him. Beat: justice assembling piece by piece.

chapters.title: Statute Expired
chapters.summary: Theo, POV. At midnight the limitation period lapses — but the attempted murder charge needs no statute, and the conspiracy unravels backward through five years. Vane is denied bail. Beat: exhausted triumph.

chapters.title: Reopening Daniel Ashford
chapters.summary: Pruitt, POV. Pruitt personally reopens the case file, attaches his own confession to obstruction, and hands the folder to the state prosecutor. The thin file grows honest pages. Beat: penance begun.

chapters.title: The Reading of the Will
chapters.summary: Theo, POV. Crane, released and dying, executes his real will: everything to Daniel's memorial foundation and an anonymous fund for witnesses like Ruth. Theo reads it aloud in the same office where the story began. Beat: full circle.

chapters.title: Alphabetized No More
chapters.summary: Theo, POV. Theo reopens his practice with a new sign and a new rule: some files are meant to be opened. He visits Daniel's grave and reports, simply, that it's finished. Beat: peace earned, not granted.

chapters.title: The Perfect Witness
chapters.summary: Vivian, POV. Months later, at Vane's trial, Vivian testifies — not as a victim but as the town's memory. Theo watches from the gallery, visible at last, and understands that witnessing is the whole job. Beat: quiet, resonant closure.
